result.title: The Neighbour's Label: Opposite Subgroup Effects of Same-Dialogue Exposure in Next-Act Evaluation
result.summary: Window-based next-act evaluation often aims to measure generalisation across dialogues, yet overlapping windows and similarity retrieval can expose labelled examples from the test dialogue. The nearest such example is the target's labelled predecessor, whose act is correct when the target continues it and wrong when the target changes act; a model that copies it can gain and lose in two subgroups that one aggregate averages. We induce this exposure under controlled designs on SGD, STAR and AMI, whose official splits are clean. Randomly including the predecessor's row in training raises a lexical classifier's continuation scores and lowers its transition scores in all three corpora, and purging the adjacent rows removes most of the gain. With TF-IDF-retrieved demonstrations, two 7B instruction-tuned models show the same opposite pattern in all eight model-corpus-sample arms (some single-cell intervals include zero; one replication is partial), while natural-weight accuracy changes by only -0.05 to +0.04. Exposure frequency depends on the retrieval pipeline. We evaluate two diagnostic comparisons without model retraining and find that excluding the test dialogue does not detectably reduce accuracy on SGD. All exposure is induced; no published system was re-evaluated.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究对话行为预测中基于窗口的 next-act 评测的「同对话暴露」问题：训练或检索中出现目标的前一条带标注样本时，复制前驱的模型会在「延续」与「转换」两个子群上呈现方向相反的效果，聚合指标将其平均掩盖；作者在 SGD、STAR、AMI 上人为诱导暴露，用词袋分类器和两个 7B 指令模型复现该模式，并做了不重训的诊断比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「检索/相似样本导致的评测泄漏」与「总体指标掩盖相反子群效应」的诊断框架，可能可供核查 LVR 中示例检索或证据获取带来的虚假增益。
